posts.body:
The agents who win in any market are the ones pricing to sell, not pricing to hope.

I've watched agents sit on listings waiting for the market to come to them. Meanwhile the agent across town prices intelligently, creates urgency, and moves inventory. When you price right from day one, you have leverage in every conversation. Sellers listen because they see momentum. Buyers show up because the numbers make sense. Other agents respect you because you close deals instead of chasing them. The market conditions don't change how this works. What changes is which agents understand that pricing strategy is the entire game.

We just wrapped a week where the team closed out deals others were sitting on. Not because we're better agents. Because we move together. One agent handled a buyer problem. Another jumped in on the inspection issue. Someone else managed the lender hiccup. That's it. That's the culture here?

I started as a solo agent convinced that high commission splits were the only reason people stuck around at brokerages. I paid out 80.20 splits thinking that's what kept agents happy. Then I watched my best people leave anyway. They didn't want more money. They wanted to not feel alone. They wanted someone to call when a deal got complicated. They wanted to be part of something that made them better. Now we run lower splits and agents stay longer because they're actually building something. The money was never the real offer. The support was. Most brokerages still don't get this.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

We're carrying more buyer and lease leads than we can work efficiently right now. New construction in San Antonio and Austin. Out-of-state relocations. They're warm leads but they need real vetting and consistent nurture before they're ready to move.

1. These aren't cold prospects. They have buying intent. They just need someone disciplined enough to stay in front of them until they actually close.

2. We can hand them off fully qualified. You're not starting from scratch. You're stepping into pipeline that's already warmed up.

3. The agent who takes this on builds their own book while we focus on what we do best.

If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

I've got agents at Lifestyle Design Realty who actually call me when things get hard instead of disappearing.

That didn't happen by accident. It happened because I stopped pretending that paychecks were the reason people stay. They stay because when a deal falls apart at 11pm, someone picks up the phone. They stay because when they're learning something new, there's a system and people to learn it from. They stay because closing a deal alone feels different than closing a deal knowing someone had your back the whole way. That's not soft stuff. That's the difference between an agent who stays two years and an agent who builds a career.

What would it feel like to work somewhere that invested in keeping you, not just recruiting you?

Top earners operate with systems, not just effort. They have lead funnels, follow-up rhythms, and accountability. They don't prospect randomly. They know their numbers. They know what converts. They build repeatable processes and then execute them daily. The gap between six figures and seven figures isn't talent. It's discipline and documentation.

I've got more buyer and lease leads sitting in our pipeline than I can efficiently work right now. New construction in San Antonio and Austin. Out-of-state relocations flowing in steady. These are warm leads with real buying intent but they need vetting and consistent nurture. Most aren't closing in thirty days. They're in the thinking phase. Planning phase. They need someone disciplined enough to stay front and center until they actually move.

The honest part. These leads won't convert themselves. They need follow-up rhythm and someone who knows how to qualify. But they're not cold. You'd be stepping into warm pipeline. Fully vetted. Already pre-qualified. You build your own book while we focus on what we do best.

If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.
